reason: Both answers are outstanding and nearly identical in structure, depth, and content. Both go well beyond the requested three problems to identify six distinct issues, including specific domain nuances like the mismatch between resident denominators and crash location numerators, bundled interventions, displacement, and heterogeneous effects. Both propose the exact same gold-standard study design (a stepped-wedge cluster randomized rollout) alongside identical quasi-experimental alternatives (even citing the same econometric estimator, Callaway-Sant'Anna). Answer A has a slightly better table mapping design choices back to the identified problems, while Answer B has a slightly better table explicitly stating the identifying assumptions of the quasi-experimental methods (which aligns well with the rubric), making them genuinely equivalent in overall quality.
